statusDefinitions.methodImplemented: A public client method exists for this operation.
statusDefinitions.typeCoverage: complete means common request and response options have dedicated exported types; partial means a generic record or escape hatch remains.
statusDefinitions.unitTests: present means at least one unit test covers the method or shared transport path; it does not mean every action is covered.
statusDefinitions.integrationTests: tested means the exact operation behavior has passed an integration test on every pinned Solr version listed as tested; partial means some versions or behavior are tested; not-run means no real Solr server test has been executed for the operation.

entries.notes: Generic SolrResponse<TDocument> and SolrQueryResponse<TDocument, TJsonFacet> types expose document metadata, classic facet counts, caller-shaped JSON facets, highlighting, grouping, stats, and debug sections. Consumer compile tests verify document inference and response-section property types. Basic query serialization and document retrieval plus cursorMark multi-page traversal are tested on the pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images; typed declarations do not certify every optional response section at runtime. Typed classic Facet Component options cover field facets and per-field limit/offset/sort/mincount/missing/prefix/method overrides, query facets, and numeric/date range facets with include/other/hardend and filter/dv methods. Solr date bucketing uses range facets; legacy facet.date parameters were removed in Solr 6. Integration coverage asserts field/query counts and numeric/date range response sections on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed highlighting options cover field selection, highlighter method, snippet/fragment sizing, field matching, alternate fields, phrase and multi-term highlighting, encoders/tags, and per-field overrides. Unit and consumer type tests cover parameter serialization and invalid values; integration tests verify returned snippets on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed Result Grouping options cover group.field, group.func, group.query, per-group limit/offset/sort, group format/main/ngroups/truncate/facet/cache settings; typed grouped response models expose matches, group counts, and per-group document lists. Typed collapse and expand options serialize the Collapsing Query Parser filter and Expand component parameters, with expanded document maps in the response. Standalone integration tests verify field grouping, group sorting, collapse selection, and expansion on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Function grouping and collapse remain subject to Solr's documented distributed/shard-local limitations. Typed Stats Component options support repeated fields, per-field local statistic selection, percentiles, cardinality, tag/key/excludeTags, global stats facets, and calcDistinct. SolrFieldStats response models include nested facet breakdowns, percentiles, and cardinality. Unit and consumer type tests cover encoding and response properties; integration tests verify numeric aggregates, distinct values/counts, cardinality, and category breakdowns on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed MoreLikeThis Search Component options cover field selection, result count, term/document-frequency thresholds, word/token/query-term limits, boosting, query fields, and interesting terms. Unit and consumer type tests cover serialization and response typing; integration tests verify similar-document results on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0.

JSON Request API query body now has a typed SolrJsonQueryRequest model and recursive JSON Facet API terms/query/range definitions, nested metrics, and domain transformations. SolrJsonQueryResponse<TDocument, TJsonFacet> exposes caller-typed facet results. Unit and consumer type tests cover nested serialization and invalid discriminators; integration tests verify terms/query/range facets, nested metrics, and excludeTags domain behavior on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Other JSON Request API options remain available through params or the legacy custom-body overload.

Document add is exercised in the CRUD smoke test on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. Named SolrUpdateOptions now expose overwrite, commitWithin, and SolrCloud _route_ serialization; request parameter serialization and invalid values are covered by unit tests. Runtime verification of route/commitWithin options remains unverified on Solr 8/9/10. Field-specific SolrAtomicUpdateOperation and SolrAtomicUpdateDocument types plus atomicUpdate() support set, add, add-distinct, remove, removeregex, and numeric inc. Unit, consumer type, and pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0 integration tests cover atomic updates. Single JSON documents use /update/json/docs; arrays use /update. Both forms are integration-tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. commitWithin is a scheduling hint whose hard/soft behavior is controlled by Solr's commitWithin configuration; the client does not force either commit type.

Replacing an existing document and reading back its updated field is tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. Atomic and JSON update commands remain unverified. Named SolrUpdateOptions now expose overwrite, commitWithin, and SolrCloud _route_ serialization; request parameter serialization and invalid values are covered by unit tests. Runtime verification of route/commitWithin options remains unverified on Solr 8/9/10. Field-specific SolrAtomicUpdateOperation and SolrAtomicUpdateDocument types plus atomicUpdate() support set, add, add-distinct, remove, removeregex, and numeric inc. Unit, consumer type, and pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0 integration tests cover atomic updates. Single JSON documents use /update/json/docs; arrays use /update. Both forms are integration-tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. commitWithin is a scheduling hint whose hard/soft behavior is controlled by Solr's commitWithin configuration; the client does not force either commit type.

Document deletion by ID is exercised in the CRUD smoke test on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. Delete-by-ID and delete-by-query serialization are covered by unit tests; SolrDeleteOptions expose route and commitWithin, with runtime verification of these request options remaining unverified on Solr 8/9/10.

Hard commit with waitSearcher is exercised by the CRUD and update integration tests on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. Command-body serialization is covered by explicit unit tests. SolrCommitOptions expose waitSearcher, softCommit, expungeDeletes (hard-commit only), and openSearcher (request parameter); integration tests cover openSearcher=false and expungeDeletes on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. Legacy CommitOptions.maxSegments is deprecated and rejected.

A newly added document becomes searchable after softCommit on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images (CI #145). Command-body serialization is covered by explicit unit tests. SolrSoftCommitOptions expose waitSearcher/openSearcher; softCommit() now waits for searcher registration by default and is integration-tested for immediate visibility on all pinned versions.

Optimize followed by query asserting committed documents remain available passed on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. SolrOptimizeOptions expose maxSegments and waitSearcher with unit and consumer type coverage; the existing optimize behavior remains integration-tested on all pinned versions. SolrOptimizeOptions expose maxSegments, waitSearcher, and openSearcher; maxSegments is optimize-only and defaults to Solr's unlimited target. The integration test exercises maxSegments on all pinned versions. openSearcher is request-parameter serialized; its optimize-specific runtime effect remains unverified.
Rollback discards a pending, uncommitted document on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images (CI #145). Command-body serialization is covered by explicit unit tests.
Ping response status OK is asserted on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images (CI #145).
Schema API add-field and GET /schema/fields read-back pass on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images; fixture cleanup deletes the field (CI #145).

Config API set-user-property plus GET /config/overlay userProps read-back pass on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images; fixture cleanup unsets the property (CI #166). Live Security API authentication and authorization checks pass in the dedicated security matrix (CI #162).
CoreAdmin CREATE, STATUS, and RELOAD pass with unique disposable cores on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images; fixture cleanup UNLOADs them (CI #145).

SolrCloud CREATE/LIST/DELETE, alias lifecycle, implicit-router shard lifecycle, named ADDREPLICA/DELETEREPLICA lifecycle, replica property add/delete and BALANCESHARDUNIQUE responses, plus multi-node MOVEREPLICA and REBALANCELEADERS leader reassignment are tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images (CI #177, #192, #209, and PR #142 CI #224). MOVEREPLICA verifies the named replica becomes active on a different live node. REBALANCELEADERS assigns preferredLeader to an active non-leader and verifies it becomes shard leader. Snapshot, backup, and cluster-state response models remain unverified.
System info metadata response passed on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images.
JVM Metrics API response passed on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. Solr 8/9 return the classic JSON registry; Solr 10.1 returns Prometheus exposition text.

Authenticated standalone BasicAuth and RuleBasedAuthorization integration tests pass on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images: anonymous rejection, authenticated configuration reads, and authentication set-property/read-back (CI #162).
Streaming Expressions search against a disposable SolrCloud collection passes on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 (CI #145).
Raw Export response with a docValues sort field passed on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images.

Generic escape hatch. It does not imply typed support for every Solr endpoint. Basic and Bearer Authorization header construction is unit-tested. The built-in transport does not log requests or add configured authorization values to error properties; custom Fetch logging and server-controlled response bodies still require caller-side redaction.

Generic raw-response escape hatch using the shared Solr transport. Supports typed methods, query parameters, headers, request bodies, cancellation, timeouts, retry policy, configured validation, and standard Solr error classes. Relative paths and same-origin absolute URLs are supported; cross-origin absolute URLs, embedded credentials, and fragments are rejected before Fetch to prevent credential leakage. String bodies are passed through unchanged when callers supply an explicit Content-Type. Custom endpoint behavior is unverified on Solr 8/9/10 until endpoint-specific integration tests are added. Basic and Bearer Authorization header construction is unit-tested. The built-in transport does not log requests or add configured authorization values to error properties; custom Fetch logging and server-controlled response bodies still require caller-side redaction.

Typed SolrJsonUpdateCommands supports add, delete, commit, optimize, and rollback command objects; command-object serialization and single/array document routing are unit, consumer-type, and pinned-version integration-tested. openSearcher values in commit/optimize command objects are extracted to the request parameter; conflicting values are rejected.
